Weak-swimming jellyfish and the Portuguese man o’ war are carried by wind, waves and currents, so they strand in seasons that follow the monsoon. The dangerous box jellyfish of the Gulf of Thailand are local residents, strong swimmers that come close to shore following food and shallow water. They have not drifted in from far away

The genus Chironex was found only from Surat Thani (about 9° N) northwards, peaked from July to September, and every severe or fatal case was in an area where Chironex occurs. This means they live and grow in the Gulf of Thailand itself, rather than drifting in from far away

Shallow water near river mouths and calm beaches need extra care

ในโลกเล็กระดับอะตอม แสงมาเป็นก้อนพลังงาน: At the scale of atoms, light comes in lumps of energy, electrons pass through walls, and things can be in several states at once until they are measured. It sounds strange, but these principles are at work in phone cameras, SSDs, TV screens, internet cables and quantum computers
1. ปรากฏการณ์โฟโตอิเล็กทริก: แสงมาเป็นก้: 1. The photoelectric effect: light comes in lumps
ถ้าแสงเป็นแค่คลื่น แสงจ้าพอก็น่าจะเตะอิเ: If light were only a wave, bright enough light should knock electrons out of a metal. But experiments found that red light never frees them however bright it is, while even dim violet light does at once. Einstein explained that light comes as photons, each with energy E = h·f, and an electron absorbs one at a time, so a single photon must be big enough (Nobel Prize 1921)

เซนเซอร์กล้องมือถือและโฟโตไดโอดปลายสายใย: Phone camera sensors and the photodiodes at the end of optical fibres use the same principle in semiconductors: a photon with more energy than the band gap (1.12 eV for silicon) releases an electron as a signal, so silicon detects light up to about 1,100 nm. Solar cells use the released electrons as electricity
2. การทะลุผ่านทางควอนตัม: อิเล็กตรอนเดิน: 2. Quantum tunnelling: electrons walking through walls
อิเล็กตรอนมีพฤติกรรมเป็นคลื่น เมื่อชนกำแ: An electron behaves like a wave. When it meets an energy barrier higher than its own energy, the wave does not stop at once but decays exponentially inside the barrier. If the barrier is thin enough, some wave is left on the other side, so the electron may appear there without climbing over. This chance is extremely sensitive to thickness: a little thicker and it drops many times
3. ควอนตัมดอต: ขนาดกำหนดสี: 3. Quantum dots: size sets the colour
อิเล็กตรอนที่ถูกขังในกล่องเล็กมีพลังงานไ: An electron trapped in a tiny box can only have certain energies (E ∝ n²/L²), like a guitar string that vibrates only at certain frequencies. The smaller the box, the further apart the levels. When the electron drops to a lower level it emits a photon whose colour matches that energy gap, so semiconductor crystals a few nanometres across (quantum dots) change colour just by changing size. They are used in QLED TVs (Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2023)

หลักเดียวกันใน LED และเลเซอร์: The same principle in LEDs and lasers
หลอด LED เลือกสีด้วยวัสดุแทนขนาด ช่องว่า: LEDs choose their colour by material rather than size: the material’s band gap sets the colour. Blue LEDs (indium gallium nitride) made today’s white LED lighting possible. A laser makes atoms emit identical photons together (stimulated emission), giving light of one colour in one direction, used to send data through fibre
4. คิวบิต: อยู่หลายสถานะพร้อมกันจนกว่าจะ: 4. Qubits: in several states at once until measured
บิตธรรมดาเป็น 0 หรือ 1 แต่คิวบิตอยู่ในสถ: An ordinary bit is 0 or 1, but a qubit can be in a superposition α|0⟩ + β|1⟩, drawn as an arrow on a sphere (the Bloch sphere) with 0 at the top and 1 at the bottom. When measured, the qubit becomes 0 or 1 at random, with probabilities |α|² and |β|². Apply the H gate twice and the state returns to 0 with certainty, because the amplitudes cancel like waves (interference). That is something a coin-flipping ordinary bit cannot do
H = ทำให้ซ้อนทับเท่า ๆ กัน · X = กลับ 0: H = equal superposition · X = swap 0 and 1 · Z = flip the sign of |1⟩ · S, T = phase rotations
คิวบิต n ตัวมีแอมพลิจูด 2ⁿ ค่าพร้อมกัน อ: n qubits hold 2ⁿ amplitudes at once. Quantum algorithms arrange for wrong answers to cancel and right answers to reinforce. Hoped-for uses include simulating molecules to design drugs and materials, and factoring numbers, which threatens today’s encryption. Real qubits are made from superconducting circuits cooled close to absolute zero, ions held by electric fields, or photons, and they lose their state very easily (decoherence)
